H_1^{\tau, \theta, (x_0, t_0)}(x,t) &:= H((t-t_0) - \theta \cdot (x - x_0)),\\

issues.failure_explanation: Writing b=t-t_0, c=θ·(x-x_0), d=θ^⊥·(x-x_0), the three wave arguments are u_1=b-c, u_2=b+c, u_3=b-d, so v_0 v_1 v_2^2 = H_3 H_1 H_2 = τ^{3/2}·(cutoffs)·exp(−τ[b²+c²+(b−d)²/2]) near (x_0,t_0). The quadratic form Q=b²+c²+(b−d)²/2 has associated matrix determinant 1/2 and is NOT the claimed isotropic form |x−x_0|²+(t−t_0)²=b²+c²+d² (e.g. along d with b=c=0 the two exponents differ by a factor 2). Consequently τ^{3/2}∫q e^{−τQ} → π^{3/2}√2·q(x_0,t_0), not π^{3/2}·q(x_0,t_0), and Lemma lemma:approx identity q (which applies only to the isotropic Gaussian e^{−τ|z−z_0|²}) cannot be invoked as done. The constant in eq: recoequ pw is therefore wrong by a factor √2.

failure_location.quote: Now, when $\tau$ is large, the product $v_0 v_1 v_2^2 \approx \tau^{\frac{3}{2}} \e^{-\tau (|x-x_0|^2 + (t-t_0)^2)}$ near the point $(x_0, t_0)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the intermediate concentration claim with the correct anisotropic quadratic form Q=b²+c²+(b−d)²/2, recompute the Gaussian integral (det = 1/2 gives π^{3/2}√2·τ^{−3/2}), and replace the constant 3!π^{3/2} in eq: recoequ pw by 3!π^{3/2}√2 (equivalently divide the right-hand side by √2). No change to the wave construction or to Lemma lemma:approx identity q is required if the anisotropic limit is computed directly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated pointwise reconstruction formula eq: recoequ pw returns √2·q(x_0,t_0) instead of q(x_0,t_0); the unregularized pointwise reconstruction comparisons in Section 4 are quantitatively biased by this constant. The qualitative claim that q(x_0,t_0) can be recovered from the DN-map up to a known normalization survives.
issues.title: Pointwise reconstruction constant wrong: wave product is anisotropic Gaussian, not isotropic
issues.why_classification: The false intermediate claim (isotropic Gaussian) is a substantive mathematical error in the derivation and Lemma lemma:approx identity q is applied outside its hypotheses, so the repair is more than a one-character typo: the concentration claim must be replaced and a Gaussian integral with a non-trivial quadratic form recomputed. However, the repair is contained within one derivation and the qualitative conclusion (pointwise recovery of q from DN data) survives with a corrected constant, so no new global proof architecture or major loss is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma is stated for non-negative integer p (so p = 0 is in scope), but C_p = (2e/p)^{−p/2} is an indeterminate expression at p = 0 (division by zero in the base). The proof's case analysis ("the maximum being (2αe/p)^{−p}") is likewise invalid at p = 0: for p = 0 the function ξ ↦ e^{−2αξ²} attains its maximum 1 at ξ = 0, so the correct constant is C_0 = 1 (obtained also by continuity of (2e/p)^{−p/2} as p → 0⁺), which is neither stated nor derived.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound in Theorem thm: reguderis error estimate for Gaussian involves the operator R^{(p)}_α, but α is never specified in the statement. Both supporting lemmas require α = δ^{2/s}, and the one-line proof simply invokes those lemmas, so the proof assumes this hypothesis without the theorem stating or deriving it. Without the constraint on α the claim is false: e.g. taking α → 0 recovers unregularized differentiation R^{(p)}_α → (∂)^p, for which ‖g^{(p)} − (∂)^p(g_δ)‖_{L²} is unbounded as a function of δ under only ‖g − g_δ‖_{L²} ≤ δ, contradicting the asserted δ^{1−p/s} rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We define the admissible reconstruction domain by setting $T>4r$, $t_1>2r$, $t_2<T-2r$, and defining $W = \Omega\times[t_1,t_2]$
Consider the recovery of the partial Radon transform \eqref{def:Radon_transform} of $q$ for a parameter tuple $(t_0, \theta_0, \eta_0)$ in the admissible reconstruction set $W_{\text{Radon}}$.
in the space domain $\Omega = [-0.5, 0.5]^2$ and time domain $[0, T] = [0, 3]$
$P$ corresponds to the interval $[-0.4, 0.4]$ divided into $63$ equally spaced distances from the origin.

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation of eq: recoequ Radon (via the Green-identity step eq: integralidentity: eps general case) requires v_0 to solve eq: wave v_0 with zero final data at t = T in Ω and v_1 to have zero initial data at t = 0 in Ω; the paper obtains these by restricting (t_0, θ_0, η_0) to W_Radon = [t_1,t_2]×S^{n−1}×[−r,r] with t_1 > 2r and t_2 < T − 2r. In Section 3.3 the parameters actually used are (t_0, θ_0, η_0) = (T/2 + η_0, θ_0, η_0) with η_0 ∈ [−0.4, 0.4]; with Ω = [−0.5, 0.5]² one has r = √2/2 ≈ 0.707, T = 3, so [t_1, t_2] ⊂ (1.414, 1.586) while t_0 = 1.5 + η_0 ∈ [1.1, 1.9]. Hence (t_0, θ_0, η_0) ∉ W_Radon for most η_0, and the specific claim v_0 = H_2 (a plane wave satisfying eq: wave v_0) is not justified. Directly, H_2(x,T) = H(−x·θ_0 − T/2 + 2η_0) is non-zero at some x ∈ Ω when |h_Ω(θ_0) − 1.5 + 2η_0| < h (e.g. η_0 near 0.4 and θ_0 near the diagonals of the square, where h_Ω(θ_0) reaches √2/2); the Green-identity boundary terms at t = T then do not vanish and eq: recoequ Radon is not established for those parameters.

failure_location.quote: More specifically, for each $\eta_0 \in P$, we set the auxiliary function $v_0$ corresponding to $(\frac{T}{2} + \eta_0, \theta_0, \eta_0)$ as in Section~\ref{sec: choosing boundary for radon}. With these choices, we can reconstruct $\radonR(q)^{\text{rec}}(\frac{T}{2} + \eta_0, \theta_0, \eta_0) = \radonR(q)^{\text{rec}}(\theta_0, \eta_0)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the reconstruction set to those (η_0, θ_0) for which (T/2+η_0, θ_0, η_0) lies in W_Radon (or, more economically, for which H_2|_{t=T} = 0 and ∂_t H_2|_{t=T} = 0 in Ω, a strictly larger set), and state the reduced coverage of each 'single-measurement' column; alternatively change the wave configuration so the intersection line stays inside [t_1, t_2] for all η_0 ∈ P (which may require more than one excitation per angle), or extend the derivation of eq: recoequ Radon to explicitly retain and control the Green-identity boundary terms at t = T when v_0 has not fully exited Ω.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that one measurement at (T/2, θ_0, 0) suffices to reconstruct 'the entire column of the sinogram corresponding to the angle θ_0' is only supported for those η_0 with (T/2+η_0, θ_0, η_0) ∈ W_Radon (roughly |η_0| < 0.086 under the stated T and Ω) — and, more generally, only where the plane waves satisfy the zero initial/final data conditions in Ω (failing near η_0 = 0.4 for diagonal θ_0). Sinogram entries outside this set, and the filtered-backprojection images built from them, are not justified by the paper's derivation. The method itself (higher-order linearization plus Gaussian focusing) and the admissible-range reconstructions are unaffected.
issues.title: Numerical reconstruction applies eq: recoequ Radon outside its admissible parameter domain
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the reconstruction range (restricting η_0 and/or θ_0 to the parameter values for which the plane waves satisfy eq: wave v_0 and the analogous initial condition) is a contained change that preserves the method and a recognizably comparable sinogram, but the advertised scope — reconstructing the entire column from one excitation over η_0 ∈ P — cannot be fully preserved without either a reconfiguration of the waves or a re-derivation that handles non-vanishing boundary terms at t = T. No global proof architecture is lost, so the issue is not serious; the loss of scope and the need for a non-trivial supporting argument place it above minor.
